clue.text: Aids zoo, fetching wild lion, say

indicators.note: wild suggests something untamed and disordered, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A zoo charity drive is boosted by bringing in a wild lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' looks like a link meaning 'bringing in', but it is part of the fodder: AIDS ZOO FETCHING gives all fifteen letters, rearranged by 'wild'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve astrological star signs, so a lion is an example.

clue.text: Car that's not hard to outstrip

parts.note: the opposite of hard is soft
to outstrip is to top, or surpass

explanation.surface: A boast that a certain car is easy to overtake.
explanation.definitionFit: A convertible car with a folding fabric roof is called by this name, so it is a type of car.

clue.text: Film star taking up old card game

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: brag is a British card game, a forerunner of poker

explanation.surface: A movie star has taken up a card game from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking up' turns the whole run O + BRAG to read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a celebrated Swedish-born Hollywood actress of the silent and early sound era.

clue.text: Unfashionable wear in the suburbs

parts.note: something unfashionable is out
skirts are items of clothing to wear

explanation.surface: Suburban dwellers are said to wear dowdy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlying districts of a city are synonymous with its suburbs.

clue.text: Aim across front of aircraft carrier

indicators.note: across means one piece stretches over the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to aim at something is to try for it

indicators.note: front of picks out the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Targeting the bow of an aircraft carrier at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aircraft carrier' reads as a ship; the definition is just 'carrier', and 'front of' gives A, set inside TRY by 'across'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is a flat board used to carry items such as food and drinks.

clue.text: Tiny page translated into ancient language

indicators.note: translated suggests the words are converted into another form, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short page of text rendered into an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the pharaohs, written in hieroglyphs, is an ancient tongue.

clue.text: Repeatedly, moderate's abandoned first

indicators.note: has abandoned its first letter, so the opening letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to moderate is to soften

explanation.surface: A moderate keeps giving up being first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the synonym has abandoned its first letter, the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something repeatedly means doing it frequently, a synonym.

clue.text: Put in grave situation without British, combined with another race

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to be put in a grave situation, i.e. buried, is to be interred

explanation.surface: A dire predicament that excludes the British, involving another race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave situation' looks like a serious plight, but literally means a burial place; 'without' means outside, so INTERRED goes around B.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that have bred across lines have been crossed with another breed or race.

clue.text: Scottish writer in English town, speaking

indicators.note: speaking says the town's name is heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: Carlisle is a town in Cumbria in northern England

explanation.surface: A Scottish author visits a town in England and gives a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is a city in north-west England near the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a nineteenth-century Scottish essayist and historian.

clue.text: To begin with, carrying advertisement for top partner

indicators.note: carrying means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to begin with means firstly

explanation.surface: A partner at the top of a firm starts by running an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a president is the partner of the top figure in a nation.

clue.text: School of trout at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shoal of trout swimming in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun for a group of fish; it is the verb meaning to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or coach them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Three horsepower vehicle

parts.note: reads as a feeble engine rated at three horsepower, but means a carriage literally pulled by three horses abreast

explanation.surface: A vehicle with a tiny engine of just three horsepower.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by a team of three horses side by side.

clue.text: Way in which poet succeeds, getting fish

indicators.note: succeeds means the poet follows the earlier pieces

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
Thomas Gray was an English poet, author of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A poet triumphs by landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous barbed tail is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Parental effort making dough

parts.note: parental can mean belonging to Pa, i.e. Pa's
an effort is a try

explanation.surface: Parents working hard at making bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like money in this context; it means a flour paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Flour, fat and water make a pastry, which is a kind of dough.

clue.text: Go to one for a change of scenery

definitions.text: Go to one for a change of scenery

parts.words: Go to one for a change of scenery
parts.note: reads as advice to take a holiday, but describes the theatre worker who shifts the sets between scenes

explanation.surface: Advice to visit someone for a change of surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre worker who moves scenery and props is literally responsible for changing scenery.

clue.text: Flying saucer that is producing gossip

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are sent spinning into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A UFO sighting that sets tongues wagging.
explanation.definitionFit: A causerie is an informal chat or chatty piece of writing, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Crazy urge plus energy —— that'll fix a lot of things!

definitions.text: that'll fix a lot of things!

indicators.note: crazy implies something disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An advert boasting that its product mends almost anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong instant adhesive is the product that repairs many broken items.

clue.text: Bloody pirate endlessly creating commotion

parts.note: bally is an old British euphemism for bloody

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A violent pirate keeps stirring up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss or uproar, a synonym for commotion.

clue.text: Money and its collector, in general? Possibly

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a hat is passed round to collect money

explanation.surface: A question of who collects the money, cash and all.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass hat is slang for a high-ranking military officer, of which a general is one example.

clue.text: May, for example, flourish without sons

indicators.note: without in its sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to flourish is to bloom
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for sons

explanation.surface: A woman called May thrives without her boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a woman's name or the month, but it is hawthorn flowers; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the hawthorn's white flowers, so it is an example of tree flowers.

clue.text: Extremely so, in this suit

parts.note: the phrase meaning in great abundance pairs the word in with this card suit

explanation.surface: A tailor praises a suit as exceedingly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four suits of playing cards, also used in the idiom meaning in abundance.

clue.text: Rose sweetly remains so, despite nominal changes

definitions.text: Rose sweetly remains so, despite nominal changes

parts.words: Rose sweetly remains so, despite nominal changes
parts.note: alludes to Romeo and Juliet: a rose by any other name would smell as sweet

explanation.surface: A rose stays fragrant whatever it is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfumed or fragrant is how Shakespeare's renamed rose would remain.

clue.text: Did excessive business, with lots of deliveries stale

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled, so overs are lots of deliveries
something stale is old

explanation.surface: A shop that sold too much and was left with stale goods after many deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sold more than can be supplied is to have done too much business.

clue.text: Someone must be able to display it

definitions.text: Someone must be able to display it

parts.words: Someone must be able to display it
parts.note: describes a quality only a capable person can show

explanation.surface: Something only a capable person can show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ability or expertise is what a capable person demonstrates.

clue.text: New partner will quickly, we hear, show resentment

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a new partner is a bride, and will said quickly is the contraction 'll, giving bride'll

explanation.surface: A newlywed will soon show annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickly' signals the shortened form 'll for will.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to bristle with anger or resentment, like a horse rearing its head.

clue.text: Follow game, neither seen nor heard

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A tracker follows the quarry silently and invisibly.
explanation.walkthrough: To lie doggo is old British slang for keeping hidden and silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggo is a slang adverb meaning hidden and quiet, so unseen and unheard.

clue.text: Piece of land providing limited parking area for Americans

parts.note: parking cut down to its abbreviation, P
in American English a lot is a ... or area of land

explanation.surface: A plot offering a small parking space for American visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a small measured area of ground, a synonym.

clue.text: Crawled, perhaps, before one religious leader

indicators.note: before places the swimming verb ahead of the next piece

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke, so crawled is an example of swam
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone crawled on their knees before a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawled' suggests grovelling; it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Escape with prince in semi-darkness

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's history plays
an escape is a flight

explanation.surface: A prince flees in the dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim light between day and night is a gloom halfway to darkness.

clue.text: Moderate place for one just passing

definitions.meaning: moderate means not extreme in views
a driver overtaking moves out into the centre of the carriageway

explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road politics avoids extremes, and the road's centre is where overtaking vehicles go.
